profile.purpose: Launch and introduce Kenji's collaboration knife with KAN, the Shitoku, by explaining its design and testing it while cooking a meal at a customer's home.
profile.thesis: The KAN x Kenji Shitoku is a hybrid of a Japanese santoku and a western gyuto, designed through several prototypes as an affordable, precise, all-purpose knife for home cooks.
key_takeaways: Kenji partnered with his friend Barney's company KAN, whose knives he bought for every cook at his restaurant about 8 years ago.
A santoku is said to have three qualities; the Shitoku ('four qualities') adds the curved, tapered tip of a gyuto (western chef's knife).
The final knife was rebalanced from the second-to-last prototype to balance at the bolster, and it was given more curve toward the tip.
It is designed for a pinch grip, and its curve and flat section support both rock chopping and Japanese-style push chopping.
Its sharpness and slight flexibility suit filleting, removing silver skin or fish skin, and thin slicing, shown on mango and tomato.
The knife has Kenji's guava pink and golden yolk banding, the KAN logo, and an egg yolk mark.
Kenji and Barney deliver one of the first finished knives to customers in Seattle and cook chanterelles, omelets and BLTs with them.
The knife is available for pre-order in limited quantities, and a portion of sales goes to charities fighting food insecurity.

outline.title: Introduction
outline.summary: Cold open of the knife delivery, then Kenji introduces himself at his home in Seattle.

outline.title: The KAN partnership and the Shitoku idea
outline.summary: Kenji explains his history with Barney's company KAN and its goal of affordable premium-feeling knives. He covers what a santoku is and how the Shitoku adds a gyuto-style tip.

outline.title: Planning the delivery
outline.summary: Kenji and Barney decide to hand-deliver one of the first finished knives to a current customer in Seattle and cook with them as a field test.

outline.title: Meeting the customers
outline.summary: They meet Sarah and Jordan, give them the knife, and look through their pantry and fridge for ingredients, including foraged chanterelles and a chili for mayo.

outline.title: Knife design and features
outline.summary: Kenji explains the hybrid shape while cutting shallots and compares the final knife to the second-to-last prototype for balance and curve. He covers the pinch grip, comfort for different hand sizes, and rock chop versus push chop.

outline.title: Cooking and knife testing
outline.summary: They mince rosemary, beat eggs and plan BLTs. Kenji demonstrates the knife's flexibility and sharpness for filleting-style cuts on a mango and thin tomato slices, and discusses the design process and the knife's colors and markings.

outline.title: Finishing the meal
outline.summary: They make omelets with sauce, assemble BLTs while discussing layering, and taste the lemony chanterelles.

outline.title: Pre-order and charity details
outline.summary: Kenji announces the knife is available for pre-order in limited quantities for holiday delivery. Barney explains that a portion of each sale goes to food insecurity charities.
